visual_description: The image is a four-panel collage showing people engaged in handcrafting drum frames using light-colored rawhide and wooden hoops. Each panel depicts individuals seated at tables, manipulating materials with their hands; tools like pliers and water bottles are visible on the tables. The bottom-left panel provides a close-up view of the woven rawhide lacing pattern across a drum hoop. No charts, tables, diagrams, labels, or numerical data are present. The layout consists of four distinct photographic scenes arranged in a grid. All images appear clear and focused on the crafting activity.

The image displays a logo for the "Healthy Brain Initiative" with the subtitle "Road Map for Indian Country." On the left side is a blue stylized icon of a human brain. To the right, the words "HEALTHY BRAIN" appear in large blue capital letters on the top line, with "INITIATIVE" directly below it in slightly smaller blue capitals. Beneath that, the phrase "Road Map for Indian Country" is written in a smaller, dark gray sans-serif font. The entire composition is set against a white background.

The image displays the logo of the National Council of Urban Indian Health. The design features a circular emblem with stylized figures representing people and urban structures, rendered in blue tones. Text encircles the central graphic, reading "NATIONAL COUNCIL OF URBAN INDIAN HEALTH" in uppercase letters. No charts, tables, axes, or numerical data are present.
